newsitem.title: FRANCE: Orangina launches plastic bottle in France.
newsitem.headline: Orangina launches plastic bottle in France.

text.p: French drinks brand Orangina, a unit of Pernod Ricard, began delivering its fizzy orange drink in plastic screw-top bottles in France this week in a bid to target younger consumers, an Orangina spokeswoman said on Friday.
The plastic bottle, the same size and shape as the "Belle Epoque"-style round glass Orangina bottle with a long neck, will gradually appear from shop shelves, she said.
"Plastic is lighter, it is a sign of the times. It corresponds to our target clientele, which is younger and younger," Francoise Beton, communication director at Orangina, told Reuters.
Orangina first tested the plastic bottle in smaller European markets to see what consumer reaction it got, and has now decided to pitch with plastic in France, its biggest market, Beton said.

The glass bottle will not disappear, but will be distributed largely to restaurants and cafes, while the plastic bottle will go to sales outlets in service stations or football stadiums, she said, adding there will be no specific advertising campaign to launch the plastic bottle.
Orangina's most recent advertising campaign, which dates from 1994 in France and 1995 internationally, put it on the map as a cult drink and brought it a range of best advertisment awards.

It is currently re-running the campaign in France on television, with its spot featuring two actors dressed up as Orangina bottles in human form who unwittingly submit to various ways of being shaken up.

The campaign for Orangina sanguine, its new red-tinged blood orange drink launched last year in France, carried on in the same vein, with the blood orange made human and cast as the villain in a murder film setting.
It is currently working on a campaign for next year with its agency, Young & Rubicam, Beton said. She declined to give any further details.
